scenes.say: Week five. Managing the evolution of brands, with Shannon Wright from Nestlé. Two brands, two paths: KitKat and Allen's.
scenes.title: Managing the evolution of brands
scenes.speaker: Shannon Wright

scenes.title: KitKat stands for *a break*
scenes.say: KitKat stands for a break, and three truths line up. The brand believes breaks are good. Everyone needs a break. And the bar is made to be broken.

scenes.kicker: The most dangerous person in marketing
scenes.say: The most dangerous person in marketing is the bored brand manager, who changes what didn't need changing. Consistency isn't limiting. It's a superpower.

scenes.kicker: The need is unchanged; the tension evolved
scenes.say: For Gen Z, sixty three percent say they need a break, but sixty four percent can't switch off. So the job is the emotional break.

stats.label: of Gen Z say they need a break

scenes.say: A debate about your brand is a jackpot. The argument over how to eat a KitKat drew twenty seven million engagements. Fan the flames.

stats.label: engagements from the *how do you eat it?* debate

note.text: Fan the flames. Don’t shut it down.

scenes.title: Mapping a brand stretch
scenes.say: Allen's wants to be a playground, not a museum. Stretch is mapped from core, to near adjacency, to credible stretch, to the exception.
The takeaway? Consistency, not sameness. Protect your assets. Use them or lose them.
